card.name: Coupe-Decale
card.tagline: Ivorian diaspora party music of flash and footwork
card.profile: Coupe-decale is an Ivorian popular dance-music genre that, per Wikipedia, was developed around 2001 by a group of young Ivorian club promoters and performers known as the Jet Set, led by Douk Saga, in Paris; Douk Saga's 'Sagacite' (2002) was the first hit of the genre. It draws heavily on Congolese ndombolo and Ivorian zouglou over deep bass and repetitive, percussive arrangements, with atalaku-style hype vocals. In Nouchi slang 'coupe' means to cheat and 'decale' to run off; the scene celebrated flamboyant dress and travaillement (throwing cash). Its dances reference everyday gestures and current events.
card.insight: Born among the Ivorian diaspora during a period of civil conflict, coupe-decale became Cote d'Ivoire's definitive pop sound and spread across Africa, later shaping Afrobeats (Wikipedia; GlobalMusix).
